ideas.name: Directional Close Location
ideas.core_thesis: A spread whose signal bar closes near the favorable end of its prior range may have cleaner directional follow-through. The target tests how favorable the close must be.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs((long direction ? feat_entryRangePosition : 100 - feat_entryRangePosition) - p); null feat_entryRangePosition or direction => -Infinity.

param.name: targetDirectionalClosePct
param.description: Target direction-aligned close location in percent; changing it tests moderate versus extreme closes.

required_features.name: feat_entryRangePosition
required_features.definition: Signal-bar close location versus the prior bar range, expressed as a percentage.

required_features.name: direction
required_features.definition: The spread direction used by the signal; long means buy BASE and sell QUOTE, while short reverses that exposure.

ideas.why_test_this: Does direction-aligned bar geometry identify the firing pair with the strongest next spread move? Shared-leg answer: a common BASE or QUOTE can give many pairs the same close-location feature, so any edge must survive selected-pair leg-reuse and leave-one-shared-leg-out checks.
ideas.how_it_fails: The close location reflects a broad market impulse or late exhaustion, so favorable-looking bars reverse instead of continuing.
ideas.clone_check: No logged rule uses pair-level entry-bar geometry; the logged rules aggregate asset votes and coverage.

ideas.name: Direction-Adjusted Gap Target
ideas.core_thesis: A gapless or directionally favorable opening may produce a cleaner spread entry than a materially adverse gap. The target allows the test to distinguish no-gap behavior from a preferred favorable gap.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs((long direction ? feat_gapPct : -feat_gapPct) - p); null feat_gapPct or direction => -Infinity.

param.name: targetDirectionalGapPct
param.description: Target gap percentage after adjusting for spread direction; zero tests gapless entries.

required_features.name: feat_gapPct
required_features.definition: This bar's pair open relative to the prior pair close, expressed as a percentage.

required_features.name: direction
required_features.definition: The spread direction used by the signal, used to make favorable and adverse gaps comparable.

ideas.why_test_this: Does the opening gap identify which firing spread has the cleanest executable entry? Shared-leg answer: one volatile leg can impose similar gaps on many pairs, so a positive result must remain after measuring whether selected pairs simply reuse that leg.
ideas.how_it_fails: The gap is an opening auction artifact, and gapless entries select inactive or already-resolved moves rather than favorable continuation.
ideas.clone_check: No logged mechanism uses per-signal pair gaps; logged gap-like coverage rules operate on asset vote density.

ideas.name: Relative ATR Cleanliness
ideas.core_thesis: Among simultaneous fires, a pair with ATR near a chosen fraction of the event's typical ATR may be cleaner than the noisiest or flattest pair. Event-median normalization makes the parameter portable across regimes.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs(feat_atrPct / median_valid_event(feat_atrPct) - p); null candidate ATR, nonpositive event median, or no valid event median => -Infinity.

param.name: targetRelativeAtr
param.description: Target ATR divided by the same-timestamp median ATR; values below one test relatively calmer spreads.

required_features.name: feat_atrPct
required_features.definition: ATR(14) divided by pair close and multiplied by 100 at the signal bar.

required_features.name: same_timestamp_candidate_pool
required_features.definition: All pairs firing at the decision timestamp, available before selection and without current or future outcomes; null values are excluded from event medians.

ideas.why_test_this: Does relative current volatility identify the cleanest spread rather than merely the loudest signal? Shared-leg answer: a low-volatility hub leg can make many pairs look clean, so leg concentration must be reported alongside the rule's result.
ideas.how_it_fails: Low ATR represents an inactive or constrained pair whose forward move is too small, while event normalization amplifies noisy median estimates.
ideas.clone_check: The logged low_volatility_thinness rule used asset-level score volatility and coverage density; this rule ranks pair-level signal ATR directly.

ideas.name: Pair Win-Rate Shrinkage
ideas.core_thesis: A pair's earlier trade win rate may predict its next spread outcome, but shallow histories should be shrunk toward the contemporaneous pair-crowd median. The single parameter controls how much history is required for trust.
ideas.selection_logic: score = (feat_pairWinRatePrior * feat_pairTradesPrior + median_valid_event(feat_pairWinRatePrior) * p) / (feat_pairTradesPrior + p); null pair history, nonpositive denominator, or no valid event median => -Infinity.

param.name: priorStrengthTrades
param.description: Pseudo-count shrinking each pair's prior win rate toward the same-timestamp median; larger values favor deeper histories.

required_features.name: feat_pairWinRatePrior
required_features.definition: Trailing win rate of this pair's earlier completed trades, null until five prior trades exist.

required_features.name: feat_pairTradesPrior
required_features.definition: Count of this pair's earlier completed trades used by the prior win-rate feature.

required_features.name: same_timestamp_candidate_pool
required_features.definition: All simultaneous firing pairs used to compute the null-filtered event median.

ideas.why_test_this: Does a pair's own earlier performance predict its next spread move after accounting for unequal history depth? Shared-leg answer: repeated success may come from repeatedly trading one hub leg, so the result must be checked for pair and leg concentration rather than accepted as independent evidence.
ideas.how_it_fails: Historical win rate is nonstationary or selected from too few trades, and shrinkage merely rewards incumbent pairs without predictive persistence.
ideas.clone_check: The logged incumbent rules used prior asset returns or asset density; this is pair-specific causal history with depth-aware shrinkage and no vote aggregation.

ideas.name: Fresh Fire Recency
ideas.core_thesis: A pair that has fired recently may be in an active, information-rich state, while a stale pair may represent an obsolete setup. The target tests which recency scale is useful.

param.name: targetBarsSinceLastFire
param.description: Target number of completed bars since this pair's preceding signal; one favors immediately fresh pairs.

required_features.name: feat_barsSincePairLastFire
required_features.definition: Number of completed bars between the signal bar and this pair's immediately preceding signal, using only prior pair signal history; null if no preceding signal exists.

ideas.why_test_this: Does a pair's own firing recency predict whether its next spread move is worth selecting? Shared-leg answer: a shared leg can cause many pairs to fire in the same burst, so freshness must be tested against the number of distinct legs represented by the selected pairs.
ideas.how_it_fails: Repeated fires are duplicate noisy signals, so recency selects crowded exposure and stale pairs would have been better contrarian candidates.
ideas.clone_check: Rookie preference in the log used incumbent history in asset-density selection; no logged rule used the pair's bars-since-last-fire state.

ideas.name: Shared-Leg Overlap Target
ideas.core_thesis: The most useful firing pair may be the one least entangled with the rest of the crowd. This directly tests whether pair selection can avoid disguising asset selection as spread selection.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs(overlapFraction - p), where overlapFraction is other firing pairs sharing BASE or QUOTE divided by the number of other firing pairs; malformed pairs or undefined fractions => -Infinity.

param.name: targetSharedLegOverlapFraction
param.description: Target fraction of same-timestamp peers sharing either leg; zero explicitly favors an isolated spread.

required_features.name: pair
required_features.definition: Canonical BASE+QUOTE identity of the firing spread, parsed into its two legs.

required_features.name: same_timestamp_candidate_pool
required_features.definition: The full set of pairs firing at this timestamp, available before selection and used to count shared-leg peers.

ideas.why_test_this: Does explicitly selecting a low-overlap pair prevent the old one-hot-asset failure? Shared-leg answer: overlap is the rule's primary defense; if every candidate shares the same hub, the rule should be reported as structurally unable to diversify rather than treated as independent pair evidence.
ideas.how_it_fails: The least-connected pair is rare, poorly observed, or has a weak signal, and overlap avoidance sacrifices the actual spread edge.
ideas.clone_check: Logged coverage-floor and rank rules measured asset coverage or vote dispersion; this rule uses canonical pair topology and never sums votes into an asset score.

ideas.name: Crowd-Relative Contrarian Gap
ideas.core_thesis: A firing pair materially below the contemporaneous crowd's direction-adjusted twenty-bar return may offer mean reversion in the spread. Median and MAD normalization make the target a crowd-relative rather than absolute return gap.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs((directionalReturn20 - median_valid_event(directionalReturn20)) / mad_valid_event(directionalReturn20) - p), where directionalReturn20 is feat_return20 for long and its negation for short; null candidate data, fewer than two valid values, or zero MAD => -Infinity.

param.name: targetReturnGapMad
param.description: Target direction-adjusted return gap in event MAD units; negative one tests a contrarian pair below the crowd median.

required_features.name: feat_return20
required_features.definition: The pair's twenty-bar return percentage at the signal bar.

required_features.name: direction
required_features.definition: The spread direction used to orient the return feature toward the trade direction.

required_features.name: same_timestamp_candidate_pool
required_features.definition: All simultaneous firing pairs used to compute the null-filtered event median and MAD.

ideas.why_test_this: Does relative underperformance versus the same-timestamp fire crowd predict a rebound in the selected spread? Shared-leg answer: common-leg moves can create apparent relative outliers, so the edge must be checked after excluding pairs that reuse the dominant leg.
ideas.how_it_fails: The underperformer is genuinely weak or structurally broken, and robust crowd normalization turns a continuation signal into a false contrarian entry.
ideas.clone_check: incumbent_reversal_tilt used prior asset returns inside density scoring; this is a direction-adjusted, same-timestamp pair-relative momentum test.

ideas.name: Crowd Range Consensus
ideas.core_thesis: The firing crowd's median direction-adjusted close location may identify a common setup state, while isolated extremes may be less reliable. The parameter tests an offset from that consensus anchor.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs(dirPos - median_valid_event(dirPos) - p), where dirPos is feat_entryRangePosition for long and 100 minus it for short; null candidate data or no valid event median => -Infinity.

param.name: targetConsensusOffsetPct
param.description: Target percentage-point offset from the same-timestamp median directional close location; zero selects consensus.

required_features.name: feat_entryRangePosition
required_features.definition: Signal-bar close location versus the prior bar range, expressed as a percentage.

required_features.name: direction
required_features.definition: The spread direction used to make close location favorable-direction aligned.

required_features.name: same_timestamp_candidate_pool
required_features.definition: All simultaneous firing pairs used to compute the null-filtered directional close-location median.

ideas.why_test_this: Does agreement with the simultaneous fire crowd outperform choosing the individually most extreme bar? Shared-leg answer: shared legs can manufacture crowd consensus, so a consensus result is only credible if selected-pair leg reuse is no higher than an appropriate crowd control.
ideas.how_it_fails: Consensus is synchronized market exposure rather than pair-specific information, and the median merely chooses the most common shared-leg setup.
ideas.clone_check: vote_dispersion_regime_switch and breadth_conditioned_regime_switch used vote-pool structure; this rule uses pair bar-location consensus and preserves pair identity.

ideas.name: Historical Spread Calm
ideas.core_thesis: A pair with stable recent spread returns may be more predictable than one experiencing unstable residual movement. This is distinct from the signal-bar ATR because it measures the pair's own preceding return path.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs(feat_pairSpreadVolatility20 / median_valid_event(feat_pairSpreadVolatility20) - p); null candidate volatility, nonpositive event median, or no valid event median => -Infinity.

param.name: targetRelativeSpreadVolatility
param.description: Target pair volatility divided by the same-timestamp median pair volatility; values below one test relatively calmer spreads.

required_features.name: feat_pairSpreadVolatility20
required_features.definition: Population standard deviation of the previous twenty one-bar percentage changes in this pair's synthetic close, using bars strictly before the signal bar; null until enough prior returns exist.

required_features.name: same_timestamp_candidate_pool
required_features.definition: All simultaneous firing pairs used to compute the null-filtered event median.

ideas.why_test_this: Does recent stability of the pair's own spread path predict its next forward spread return? Shared-leg answer: a common calm leg can make many pair histories look stable, so selected-pair concentration and a leave-one-leg-out result are mandatory checks.
ideas.how_it_fails: Calmness selects dead or mean-reverting pairs with little opportunity, while volatility clustering makes the historical window stale at the decision bar.
ideas.clone_check: low_volatility_thinness and zero_variance_plateau_discount used asset-level score or coverage behavior; this rule uses causal realized volatility of each pair's synthetic spread.

ideas.name: Hedge Volatility Balance
ideas.core_thesis: A spread whose BASE and QUOTE legs have comparable recent volatility may be less dominated by one leg. Targeting a ratio other than one tests whether intentional asymmetry is more useful than balance.
ideas.selection_logic: score = -abs(ln(feat_legVolatilityRatio20 / p)); null or nonpositive leg-volatility ratio, or nonpositive p => -Infinity.

param.name: targetBaseQuoteVolRatio
param.description: Target recent BASE volatility divided by QUOTE volatility; one tests balanced legs.

required_features.name: feat_legVolatilityRatio20
required_features.definition: Population standard deviation of the prior twenty one-bar percentage returns of BASE divided by the corresponding value for QUOTE, using only bars strictly before the signal bar; null unless both are available and QUOTE volatility is positive.

ideas.why_test_this: Does hedge-leg volatility balance identify a cleaner tradeable spread? Shared-leg answer: a hub leg can make the same ratio recur across many pairs, so any apparent balance edge must be checked for BASE or QUOTE reuse and residual pair uniqueness.
ideas.how_it_fails: Volatility balance does not imply cointegration or mean reversion, and the ratio ignores the direction and covariance that determine actual spread risk.
ideas.clone_check: No logged idea used the volatility relationship between a pair's two legs; the closest logged volatility rules were asset-vote or score-volatility rules.
